speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a neck swelling; can you tell me how long it has been present and if you've noticed any pain, fever, or weight loss? Also, has this swelling changed in size recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that detailed history; given your history of colon cancer, are you aware of any recent changes in bowel habits, night sweats, or persistent cough? Additionally, has the swelling become firm or fixed to the underlying structures?

REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, TSH, and Thyroglobulin antibodies.
REQUEST IMAGES: Neck_Ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CBC: Normal WBC, Hemoglobin, Platelets; ESR: Not Provided; TSH: Not Provided; Thyroglobulin antibodies: Not Provided; Neck_Ultrasound: Well-circumscribed lesion in the subcutaneous tissue suggestive of a cystic nature.
